workflow.name: ERC-3643 Production Conformance Review
workflow.description: A focused first-pass workflow that builds one authoritative requirement catalogue from the official ERC-3643 specification and its referenced interfaces, maps production-reachable components, routes each component through six applicable conformance areas, and independently adjudicates and deduplicates proven deviations. Zero terminal records means no normative deviation was proven; it does not establish full compliance, and professional auditor review remains required.

steps.name: Establish Shared Normative Catalogue
steps.content:
Objective: establish the single shared ERC-3643 requirement catalogue that every later mapping, review, and adjudication step must use.

Available inputs: repository {{repo_full}} at {{commit_sha}}; scope {{repo_scope}}; declared dependencies {{dependencies}}; configuration {{configuration}}; workspace root {{workspace_root}}; layout {{workspace_layout}}; manifest {{workspace_manifest_json}}.

Official normative sources:

* ERC-3643 specification: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643
* Official ERC-3643 interfaces linked from that specification under https://eips.ethereum.org/assets/eip-3643/
* ERC-20: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-20
* ERC-173: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-173
* The ONCHAINID interfaces directly referenced by ERC-3643, only where needed to interpret ERC-3643 identity and claim verification.

Prefer an official local snapshot when one is supplied and record its repository commit or revision. Otherwise use the official URLs above. If neither the official sources nor a supplied snapshot can be accessed, mark the affected requirements unresolved_source. Never reconstruct normative requirements from the audited implementation or the T-REX reference implementation.

Repository code, comments, tests, examples, rationale, optional behavior, preferred architecture, legal-policy assumptions, and general security practice are not normative sources.

Build one record per atomic binding obligation. Cover every explicit MUST and MUST NOT and every binding behavior or required declaration concerning: ERC-20 compatibility; transfer and transferFrom; free balance; sender and receiver freeze status; pause status; receiver verification; compliance approval and post-transfer notification; onchain identity integration; wallet registration; Identity lookup; required Claim Topics; valid claims; authorized Trusted Issuers; configurable compliance; compliance binding; canTransfer; transferred, created and destroyed callbacks; mint; burn; forcedTransfer; recovery; partial and total freezing; pause/unpause; Owner and Agent authority; registries; Identity Registry Storage; getters; events; and batch variants.

Distinguish mandatory behavior from optional capabilities. For example, Identity Registry Storage may support several bound Identity Registries, but do not require every implementation or deployment to actually share storage unless the official text makes that behavior mandatory.

Treat functions, getters, events and externally observable signatures required by the official interfaces as conformance obligations. Evaluate compatibility according to Solidity and ABI semantics. Do not require identical source syntax, parameter names, declaration order, or an `external` declaration when a compatible `public` implementation satisfies the interface. Require the correct externally observable selector, ABI parameter and return types, state mutability and event signature. Treat event emission as mandatory only when the official specification defines that behavioral obligation; the presence of an event declaration alone does not prove correct emission.

Use these fixed behavioral prefixes: REQ-ERC20, REQ-XFER, REQ-XFERFROM, REQ-IDENTITY, REQ-CLAIM, REQ-REGISTRY, REQ-STORAGE, REQ-COMPLIANCE, REQ-MINT, REQ-BURN, REQ-FORCED, REQ-RECOVERY, REQ-FREEZE, REQ-PAUSE, REQ-ROLE and REQ-BATCH. Number atomic clauses within each family in official-source order using three digits, such as REQ-XFER-001.

Give interface declarations deterministic IDs of the form REQ-IFACE-<OFFICIAL_INTERFACE>-<FUNCTION_OR_EVENT_NAME>-<three-digit declaration order>. Use official declaration order and never renumber requirements based on repository contents. Preserve one principal ID per materially separable obligation; related requirements may be cited as supporting requirements.

For each record return:

* catalog_requirement_id
* catalog_domain
* catalog_obligation
* catalog_obligation_kind as MUST, MUST_NOT, BINDING_BEHAVIOR, FUNCTION_SIGNATURE, EVENT_SIGNATURE, or GETTER_SIGNATURE
* catalog_normative_source
* catalog_source_anchor
* catalog_applicability
* catalog_required_signatures
* catalog_required_events
* catalog_status as established or unresolved_source
* catalog_uncertainty

catalog_obligation must precisely paraphrase the official requirement without adding policy. catalog_source_anchor must identify the official section, declaration or signature and its stable URL, path, revision or commit. Signature and event arrays must contain exact ABI-relevant signatures or be empty when inapplicable.

An established record requires direct support from the official normative corpus. If the source, normative strength or exact declaration cannot be verified, emit unresolved_source and identify the missing evidence precisely. Do not turn rationale, examples, optional features or implementation behavior into binding requirements. Emit no invented obligations and no aggregate placeholder instead of atomic records.

steps.name: Map Production-Reachable ERC-3643 Components
steps.content:
Objective: map the concrete production-reachable components that implement or materially determine ERC-3643 behavior, and bind each component to the applicable records from the shared normative catalogue before behavioral review.

Shared catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}. Repository inputs: {{repo_full}} at {{commit_sha}}; scope {{repo_scope}}; dependencies {{dependencies}}; configuration {{configuration}}; workspace root {{workspace_root}}; layout {{workspace_layout}}; manifest {{workspace_manifest_json}}.

Inspect production source, deployment scripts and manifests, factories, constructors and initializers, proxy implementations and upgrade paths, inheritance and overrides, linked libraries, role assignment, Identity Registry, Identity Registry Storage, Claim Topics Registry, Trusted Issuers Registry, compliance contracts and modules, identity contracts, dependencies, configuration gates, and cross-contract wiring.

Treat a component as production-reachable when checked-out source and supplied repository or configuration evidence show that it can execute as part of an in-scope deployable or deployed ERC-3643 system. An actual mainnet deployment is not required unless the supplied scope claims conformance for a specific deployment. Distinguish deployed, deployable, conditionally reachable and unresolved paths.

Exclude tests, mocks, examples, benchmarks, developer-only deployments and dead alternatives unless supplied configuration proves they are active. Include external or inherited dependencies only when their runtime behavior materially determines an in-scope ERC-3643 obligation. Do not create separate records for passive interfaces or unrelated helper contracts.

Emit one record per independently reviewable production-facing component or implementation unit. Do not combine unrelated contracts. Assign mapped_component_id from the component’s ERC-3643 role and source symbol, not discovery order.

For each component identify:

* Exact source location and primary symbol.
* Production-facing entrypoints.
* Proxy, delegatecall, inheritance and library implementation chain.
* Constructor, initializer and upgrade path.
* Owner, Agent and other relevant actors.
* Dependencies and trusted external components.
* Concrete registry, identity and compliance wiring.
* Actor-controlled arguments or state.
* Exact evidence supporting production reachability.
* Applicable catalogue requirements and review areas.

Select mapped_applicable_requirement_ids only from established records in the supplied catalogue. Later review steps should consume this filtered subset rather than reconstructing the standard or repeatedly receiving the entire catalogue.

Route requirements only to these review areas:

* transfers_erc20
* identity_claims_registries
* compliance_callbacks
* privileged_token_operations
* recovery_freeze_pause
* roles_interfaces_batches

Determine applicability from the ERC-3643 role that the component or assembled system claims to fulfil, not merely from the functions currently present in its source. A missing required function, interface, component or execution path must not cause its catalogue requirement to be omitted or marked not applicable. Route the requirement to the production-facing component responsible for providing the expected behavior so later review can determine whether its absence is a deviation.

In particular, route required Token interface obligations to the production-facing token even when a selector is absent. Route registry, identity, compliance and role obligations to the component responsible for that standard role. If an entire required subsystem appears absent, associate the relevant integration requirement with the main ERC-3643 token or system assembly and record the missing link as mapping uncertainty; do not conclude a deviation during mapping.

Interface declarations establish the expected surface but do not prove that deployed selectors or runtime behavior conform. Conversely, absence of an expected declaration or component is routing evidence, not a reason to suppress the requirement.

Return mapped_scope_status as reachable, deployable, conditionally_reachable or unresolved. Use mapped_uncertainty only for concrete missing deployment, proxy, initialization, dependency, configuration or wiring evidence. Do not use uncertainty to hide an observable absence from the production-facing surface.

Evidence must cite exact paths, lines, symbols, deployment facts, configuration keys, storage-slot observations or ordered wiring locations. Names, comments and interface inheritance alone are insufficient proof of runtime conformity.

Before finishing, reconcile the established catalogue against all mapped records. Every mandatory requirement applicable to the claimed ERC-3643 system must be assigned to at least one responsible component. If responsibility cannot be resolved, route it to the main system assembly and record the ambiguity. If no production-reachable or deployable ERC-3643 system can be supported, emit zero records rather than mapping examples or assumptions.

steps.name: Review Transfers and ERC-20 Behavior
steps.content:
Objective: assess the transfers_erc20 requirements applicable to this mapped production component.

Shared normative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}.
Routed requirement IDs: {{mapped_applicable_requirement_ids}}.

Use only the catalogue records whose catalog_requirement_id appears in mapped_applicable_requirement_ids. Ignore unrelated catalogue records and do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643.

Component context: ID {{mapped_component_id}}; label {{mapped_component_label}}; kind {{mapped_component_kind}}; source {{mapped_source_location}}; production entrypoints {{mapped_production_entrypoints}}; implementation chain {{mapped_implementation_chain}}; initialization {{mapped_initialization_path}}; roles {{mapped_roles}}; dependencies {{mapped_dependencies}}; wiring {{mapped_wiring}}; actor-controlled inputs {{mapped_actor_inputs}}; reachability evidence {{mapped_reachability_evidence}}; routed areas {{mapped_applicable_review_areas}}; scope status {{mapped_scope_status}}; uncertainty {{mapped_uncertainty}}.

If transfers_erc20 is not routed and no concrete evidence makes its applicability ambiguous, emit zero records. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643. Use only the supplied applicable requirement records and their normative meanings.

Trace the complete production execution of transfer and transferFrom from caller-controlled addresses and amounts through:

* ERC-20 caller and allowance handling.
* Sender balance and free balance: total balance minus frozen tokens.
* Partial-token freezing.
* Total freeze status of sender and receiver.
* Token pause status.
* Receiver registration and identity verification.
* Compliance canTransfer decision.
* Balance and allowance mutations.
* Transfer event and return/revert behavior.
* Required post-transfer compliance notification.

Assess transfer and transferFrom separately wherever their caller, allowance or execution paths differ. Verify that transferFrom preserves every ERC-3643 transfer restriction applicable to transfer while also satisfying the catalogued ERC-20 allowance behavior.

Do not require sender identity verification unless an applicable catalogue requirement expressly requires it. Do not import mint, burn, forcedTransfer, recovery or batch semantics into ordinary transfers.

Distinguish the scope of the compliance pre-check from the complete set of conditions that can make a token transfer fail. Do not assume that canTransfer returning true guarantees successful execution when balance, allowance, pause, freeze or identity conditions are checked separately. Compare the implementation only against the precise pre-check guarantee established in the shared catalogue. If the official sources leave that relationship ambiguous, record unresolved rather than selecting the stricter interpretation.

Compare all applicable ERC-20 and ERC-3643 requirements against both the production-facing ABI and the executable implementation. Apply Solidity and ABI compatibility rather than textual equality: compatible public implementations of external interface functions are acceptable, and parameter names or source declaration order are irrelevant.

A matching interface declaration, inherited signature or ABI selector does not prove correct runtime behavior. Conversely, a missing or ABI-incompatible required production-facing function can be a possible_deviation without an exploit.

Emit one record per applicable atomic requirement with assessment_disposition equal to:

* compliant
* possible_deviation
* not_applicable
* unresolved

Use not_applicable only when evidence proves that the requirement does not apply to this component while remaining assigned elsewhere where required. Do not use it merely because an expected function or check is absent.

Keep compliant records concise. For possible_deviation, provide the exact requirement ID and source, expected and observed behavior, exact source locations, complete production execution path, minimal state and call sequence, actor and controlled input, counterchecks, practical conformance impact, exploitability and remaining uncertainty.

Countercheck inherited implementations, modifiers, hooks, internal transfer functions, proxy dispatch, alternate entrypoints, allowance branches, zero-value transfers, revert paths, compliance callbacks and configured registry/compliance addresses.

Do not report reentrancy, accounting, economic, governance, access-control or policy concerns unless they directly establish a supplied catalogue violation. If any necessary normative, deployment, wiring or execution link remains unsupported, use unresolved rather than possible_deviation.

steps.name: Review Identity, Claims, and Registries
steps.content:
Objective: assess the identity_claims_registries requirements applicable to this mapped production component.

Shared normative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}. Routed requirement IDs: {{mapped_applicable_requirement_ids}}.

Use only catalogue records whose catalog_requirement_id appears in mapped_applicable_requirement_ids and whose domain is relevant to identity_claims_registries. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643.

Component context: ID {{mapped_component_id}}; label {{mapped_component_label}}; kind {{mapped_component_kind}}; source {{mapped_source_location}}; production entrypoints {{mapped_production_entrypoints}}; implementation chain {{mapped_implementation_chain}}; initialization {{mapped_initialization_path}}; roles {{mapped_roles}}; dependencies {{mapped_dependencies}}; wiring {{mapped_wiring}}; actor-controlled inputs {{mapped_actor_inputs}}; reachability evidence {{mapped_reachability_evidence}}; routed areas {{mapped_applicable_review_areas}}; scope status {{mapped_scope_status}}; uncertainty {{mapped_uncertainty}}.

If identity_claims_registries is not routed and no concrete evidence makes its applicability ambiguous, emit zero records. Do not mark a requirement not applicable merely because an expected registry, function, binding or verification step is absent.

Trace the complete production isVerified pipeline:

1. Determine whether the wallet is registered in the applicable Identity Registry.
2. Resolve the wallet to its configured Identity contract and country data.
3. Obtain every Claim Topic required by the configured Claim Topics Registry.
4. Retrieve the Identity claims relevant to each required topic.
5. Identify the issuer associated with each claim.
6. Confirm that the issuer is registered as a Trusted Issuer for that specific Claim Topic.
7. Validate the claim using the signature, data and validity mechanism required by the official ERC-3643 and referenced ONCHAINID interfaces.
8. Confirm that isVerified returns the catalogue-required result and that token operations consume that result where required.

Distinguish these separate conditions:

* A wallet being present in storage does not by itself prove that it is verified.
* A claim existing does not prove that it is valid.
* An issuer being trusted for one topic does not make it trusted for every topic.
* A valid claim for one required topic does not satisfy other required topics.
* Multiple authorized issuers for one topic represent alternative valid issuers only when the catalogue supports that interpretation.

Apply the exact conjunction and alternative-issuer semantics established by the catalogue. Do not invent behavior for an empty Claim Topics Registry, missing issuers, duplicate topics or multiple claims where the official sources do not determine the result; classify genuinely ambiguous cases as unresolved.

Review the production behavior of:

* Identity Registry registration, update, deletion and lookup.
* Wallet-to-Identity and wallet-to-country consistency.
* Identity Registry setters and configured dependencies.
* Identity Registry Storage addition, removal and modification.
* Binding and unbinding of Identity Registries to shared storage.
* Claim Topics Registry additions, removals and queries.
* Trusted Issuers Registry additions, removals, topic updates and queries.
* The effect of registry and issuer changes on subsequent verification.
* Required authorization, getters and events.
* Identity-specific batch operations where their semantics are catalogued.

Treat shared Identity Registry Storage as an available standardized capability, not as a requirement that every deployment must share storage, unless the applicable catalogue record expressly requires it.

Trace mutations and subsequent reads across contract boundaries. Check for stale or inconsistent relationships after identity replacement, identity removal, country modification, topic removal, issuer removal, issuer-topic updates, storage rebinding and registry replacement. These state transitions are relevant only where they cause a supplied catalogue obligation to be violated.

Compare applicable official interface obligations against the production-facing ABI and executable implementation using Solidity and ABI compatibility. Do not require identical source syntax or parameter names. A matching interface declaration does not prove correct execution; a missing or incompatible required selector may be a possible_deviation without an exploit.

Emit one record per applicable atomic requirement with assessment_disposition equal to compliant, possible_deviation, not_applicable or unresolved.

Use not_applicable only when evidence proves that the requirement belongs to another mapped component or does not apply to the claimed role. Keep compliant records concise. A possible_deviation must include the exact requirement ID and source, expected and observed behavior, ordered cross-contract path, exact evidence locations, minimal pre-state and call sequence, actor and controlled input, counterchecks, proportionate impact, exploitability and remaining uncertainty.

Countercheck inherited logic, proxy dispatch, registry replacement, storage binding, alternative trusted issuers, multiple claims, invalid or removed claims, configuration gates and token-side consumption of isVerified.

Do not derive requirements from KYC policy preferences, legal assumptions, implementation conventions or the T-REX reference implementation. If claim validity, normative meaning, production wiring or deployment state cannot be established, use unresolved rather than possible_deviation.

steps.name: Review Compliance and State Callbacks
steps.content:
Objective: assess the compliance_callbacks requirements applicable to this mapped production component.

Shared normative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}. Routed requirement IDs: {{mapped_applicable_requirement_ids}}.

Use only catalogue records whose catalog_requirement_id appears in mapped_applicable_requirement_ids and whose domain is relevant to compliance_callbacks. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643.

Component context: ID {{mapped_component_id}}; label {{mapped_component_label}}; kind {{mapped_component_kind}}; source {{mapped_source_location}}; production entrypoints {{mapped_production_entrypoints}}; implementation chain {{mapped_implementation_chain}}; initialization {{mapped_initialization_path}}; roles {{mapped_roles}}; dependencies {{mapped_dependencies}}; wiring {{mapped_wiring}}; actor-controlled inputs {{mapped_actor_inputs}}; reachability evidence {{mapped_reachability_evidence}}; routed areas {{mapped_applicable_review_areas}}; scope status {{mapped_scope_status}}; uncertainty {{mapped_uncertainty}}.

If compliance_callbacks is not routed and no concrete evidence makes its applicability ambiguous, emit zero records. Do not mark a requirement not applicable merely because the expected compliance contract, binding, function or callback is absent.

Establish the complete production relationship between the Token and Compliance components:

* Which Compliance implementation is configured.
* How the Token and Compliance addresses are set, bound, replaced or unbound.
* Which actors may perform those operations.
* Whether both sides of the relationship remain consistent.
* Which proxy, initializer, factory or upgrade path determines the active wiring.
* Whether the inspected rules or modules are actually active in production.

Trace ordinary transfer and transferFrom through two distinct stages:

1. Pre-transfer decision through canTransfer.
2. Post-operation synchronization through transferred.

For each stage verify the caller, `_from`, `_to` and `_amount` values, call order, return-value propagation, revert behavior and relationship with the actual token state transition. Confirm that a rejected compliance decision prevents the transfer wherever required and that successful operations invoke the catalogued callback with values corresponding to the movement actually performed.

Trace mint, burn and forcedTransfer separately through their applicable created, destroyed or transferred callbacks. Apply only the checks, callbacks and compliance bypasses established in the catalogue. Do not apply ordinary-transfer canTransfer requirements to mint, burn or forcedTransfer when the standard permits them to bypass those rules. A permitted pre-check bypass does not imply that a required post-operation state-synchronization callback may also be skipped.

For every applicable operation determine:

* Whether canTransfer is called when required.
* Whether the correct Compliance instance is called.
* Whether its result is enforced.
* Whether the state transition occurs before or after the callback as required.
* Whether the appropriate callback executes exactly as required after a successful operation.
* Whether callbacks are skipped or rolled back on reverted operations.
* Whether callback parameters represent the actual operation.
* Whether callback failure reverts or is ignored, but only when the catalogue defines that behavior.
* Whether alternate entrypoints, batches or inherited paths bypass required checks or notifications.

Review the authorization of bindToken, unbindToken and state-changing callbacks only where the catalogue makes the caller restriction binding. Do not infer an `onlyToken`, `onlyOwner` or modular-access rule solely from the T-REX implementation or general security expectations.

Assess configurable compliance at the capability and integration level required by ERC-3643. Do not require a particular module architecture, module collection or legal rule. A custom Compliance implementation and a modular implementation may both conform if they satisfy the catalogued interface and behavior.

Check applicable production-facing getters, setters, events, function signatures, return types and mutability using Solidity and ABI compatibility. In particular, verify the catalogued read-only behavior of canTransfer without demanding identical source syntax. Interface declarations or matching selectors do not prove correct binding, decision propagation or state synchronization.

Emit one record per applicable atomic requirement with assessment_disposition equal to compliant, possible_deviation, not_applicable or unresolved.

Use not_applicable only when evidence proves that the requirement belongs to another mapped component or operation. Keep compliant records concise. For possible_deviation provide the exact requirement ID and source, expected and observed behavior, precise evidence locations, ordered cross-contract execution path, minimal pre-state and call sequence, actor and controlled input, counterchecks, proportionate interoperability or compliance-state impact, exploitability and remaining uncertainty.

Countercheck proxy dispatch, inherited overrides, compliance replacement, stale binding, direct callback access, failed and successful operations, callback reverts, alternate transfer entrypoints, batch routing and permitted bypasses. Treat a difference as a candidate only when it violates the supplied catalogue rather than a preferred integration model.

If the normative meaning, active Compliance implementation, binding, configuration or execution path cannot be proven, use unresolved rather than possible_deviation.

steps.name: Review Privileged Token Operations
steps.content:
Objective: assess the privileged_token_operations requirements applicable to this mapped production component.

Shared normative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}. Routed requirement IDs: {{mapped_applicable_requirement_ids}}.

Use only catalogue records whose catalog_requirement_id appears in mapped_applicable_requirement_ids and whose domain is relevant to privileged_token_operations. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643.

Component context: ID {{mapped_component_id}}; label {{mapped_component_label}}; kind {{mapped_component_kind}}; source {{mapped_source_location}}; production entrypoints {{mapped_production_entrypoints}}; implementation chain {{mapped_implementation_chain}}; initialization {{mapped_initialization_path}}; roles {{mapped_roles}}; dependencies {{mapped_dependencies}}; wiring {{mapped_wiring}}; actor-controlled inputs {{mapped_actor_inputs}}; reachability evidence {{mapped_reachability_evidence}}; routed areas {{mapped_applicable_review_areas}}; scope status {{mapped_scope_status}}; uncertainty {{mapped_uncertainty}}.

If privileged_token_operations is not routed and no concrete evidence makes its applicability ambiguous, emit zero records. Do not mark an obligation not applicable merely because an expected privileged function or execution path is absent.

Review mint, burn and forcedTransfer as three distinct operation families. Do not transfer checks or permitted bypasses from one family to another unless the supplied catalogue expressly connects them.

For mint, trace:

* The actor authorized to call mint.
* Recipient and amount handling.
* Required receiver registration and identity verification.
* Supply and recipient-balance mutation.
* Compliance pre-check bypass or enforcement exactly as catalogued.
* Required created callback.
* Required ERC-20 and ERC-3643 events.
* Pause, freeze and revert behavior only where catalogued.

For burn, trace:

* The actor authorized to call burn.
* Holder and amount handling.
* Holder balance, frozen-token accounting and total-supply mutation.
* The catalogue-defined bypass of eligibility checks.
* Required destroyed callback.
* Required ERC-20 and ERC-3643 events.
* Pause, freeze and revert behavior only where catalogued.

Do not require the burned holder to remain verified when the catalogue establishes that burn bypasses eligibility. Do not assume how frozen-token state must be adjusted unless the normative catalogue defines that behavior.

For forcedTransfer, trace:

* The Agent or other catalogue-authorized caller.
* The distinction between the caller and the `_from` token holder.
* Source, destination and amount handling.
* Required destination registration and identity verification.
* Source balance and frozen-token accounting.
* Compliance pre-check bypass or enforcement exactly as catalogued.
* Required transferred callback.
* Balance mutation, events and return/revert behavior.
* Pause and freeze interactions only where catalogued.

Interpret “force transfers from an Agent wallet” according to the catalogue and official context. Do not assume that `_from` must be the Agent’s own token-holding address merely because the Agent wallet initiates the call. Verify caller authority and token source as separate properties.

For all three operation families:

* Trace the production-facing selector through proxy, inheritance, modifiers, internal helpers and cross-contract calls.
* Verify that the active role restriction matches the relevant catalogue obligation.
* Verify actual state changes rather than relying on interface declarations.
* Compare callback parameters with the operation actually performed.
* Check successful, rejected and partially constrained pre-states.
* Distinguish required recipient verification from compliance-rule enforcement.
* Apply Solidity and ABI compatibility rather than textual source equality.
* Assess batch behavior only where needed to determine whether the single-operation semantics are preserved; leave generic batch-interface coverage to roles_interfaces_batches.

A permitted compliance bypass is not a deviation. Conversely, a bypass of identity, authorization, accounting or callback behavior may be a possible_deviation only when that requirement appears in the routed catalogue. Do not infer that bypassing canTransfer also permits omission of a separately required created, destroyed or transferred callback.

Emit one record per applicable atomic requirement with assessment_disposition equal to compliant, possible_deviation, not_applicable or unresolved.

Use not_applicable only when evidence proves that the requirement belongs to another component or operation. Keep compliant records concise. A possible_deviation must include the exact requirement ID and source, expected and observed behavior, precise source locations, ordered execution path, minimal pre-state and call sequence, actor and controlled input, counterchecks, proportionate conformance impact, exploitability and remaining uncertainty.

A deviation may concern behavior executed by an authorized Owner or Agent and need not be exploitable by an untrusted caller. Identify the actual required actor and do not label privileged standard functionality itself as a vulnerability.

Countercheck alternate entrypoints, internal helpers, inherited overrides, proxy dispatch, role changes, zero amounts, insufficient balances, frozen balances, unverified recipients, compliance bypasses, callback failures, reverts and batch wrappers.

If the normative rule, authorization model, active implementation, configuration, wiring or execution result cannot be proven, use unresolved rather than possible_deviation.

steps.name: Review Recovery, Freeze, and Pause Controls
steps.content:
Objective: assess the recovery_freeze_pause requirements applicable to this mapped production component.

Shared normative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}. Routed requirement IDs: {{mapped_applicable_requirement_ids}}.

Use only catalogue records whose catalog_requirement_id appears in mapped_applicable_requirement_ids and whose domain is relevant to recovery_freeze_pause. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643.

Component context: ID {{mapped_component_id}}; label {{mapped_component_label}}; kind {{mapped_component_kind}}; source {{mapped_source_location}}; production entrypoints {{mapped_production_entrypoints}}; implementation chain {{mapped_implementation_chain}}; initialization {{mapped_initialization_path}}; roles {{mapped_roles}}; dependencies {{mapped_dependencies}}; wiring {{mapped_wiring}}; actor-controlled inputs {{mapped_actor_inputs}}; reachability evidence {{mapped_reachability_evidence}}; routed areas {{mapped_applicable_review_areas}}; scope status {{mapped_scope_status}}; uncertainty {{mapped_uncertainty}}.

If recovery_freeze_pause is not routed and no concrete evidence makes its applicability ambiguous, emit zero records. Do not mark a requirement not applicable merely because an expected function, control or execution path is absent.

Review recovery, partial token freezing, total address freezing and pausing as distinct control families. Do not transfer behavior between them unless the supplied catalogue expressly connects the requirements.

For wallet recovery, trace:

* The actor authorized to initiate recovery.
* The lost wallet, replacement wallet and investor onchain Identity inputs.
* Required preconditions concerning the old and new wallet.
* The relationship between the supplied Identity and the Identity Registry.
* Country and registry updates where catalogued.
* Balance movement from the lost wallet to the replacement wallet.
* Frozen-token and total-freeze state handling where catalogued.
* Required compliance interaction or permitted bypass.
* Removal, replacement or preservation of the lost-wallet registry association.
* Required RecoverySuccess or other catalogued events.
* The onchain history required to demonstrate that recovery occurred.
* The final state of both wallet addresses after completion or revert.

Do not assume that recovery must migrate ERC-20 allowances, permits, nonces, votes, delegation or unrelated auxiliary state unless an applicable catalogue requirement explicitly says so. Do not treat the exact recovery sequence used by T-REX as mandatory. Evaluate the externally required result defined by ERC-3643.

For partial freezing and unfreezing, trace:

* Authorized caller.
* Target wallet and amount.
* Stored frozen-token amount before and after the operation.
* Free balance available for ordinary transfers.
* Required amount bounds and revert behavior.
* Required TokensFrozen and TokensUnfrozen events.
* Sequential freezes and unfreezes.
* Interaction with transfer, burn, forcedTransfer and recovery only where catalogued.

Check whether multiple operations preserve the relationship between total balance, frozen tokens and transferable free balance. Do not impose a particular over-freeze, underflow or automatic-unfreeze policy unless the catalogue establishes it.

For total address freezing and unfreezing, trace:

* Authorized caller.
* Target address and stored freeze status.
* Required AddressFrozen event.
* Enforcement against the sender and receiver of ordinary transfers.
* Restoration of transfer eligibility after unfreezing.
* Interaction with partial freezing and privileged operations only where catalogued.

Treat total address freeze and partial-token freeze as separate state dimensions unless the normative catalogue defines a stronger relationship.

For pause and unpause, trace:

* Authorized caller.
* Stored pause state and required events.
* Enforcement against every operation explicitly conditioned on pause by the catalogue.
* Restoration of the required behavior after unpausing.
* Alternate, inherited and internal entrypoints that may bypass the pause check.

Do not assume that mint, burn, forcedTransfer, recovery or every privileged operation must be blocked while paused unless the catalogue expressly requires it. The explicit pause rule for ordinary transfers must not automatically be generalized.

For all control families:

* Follow proxy dispatch, inherited modifiers, internal helpers and cross-contract registry or compliance calls.
* Compare the production-facing ABI and executable behavior with applicable catalogue requirements.
* Apply Solidity and ABI compatibility rather than textual equality.
* Verify state transitions and events on both successful and reverted paths.
* Assess batch variants only where needed to determine preservation of the single-operation semantics; leave generic batch coverage to roles_interfaces_batches.

A matching function or interface declaration does not prove correct runtime behavior. A missing or incompatible required function may be a possible_deviation without an untrusted exploit.

Emit one record per applicable atomic requirement with assessment_disposition equal to compliant, possible_deviation, not_applicable or unresolved.

Use not_applicable only when evidence proves that the requirement belongs to another component or operation. Keep compliant records concise. A possible_deviation must include the exact requirement ID and source, expected and observed behavior, precise evidence locations, complete execution path, minimal pre-state and call sequence, actor and controlled input, counterchecks, proportionate conformance impact, exploitability and remaining uncertainty.

A deviation reachable only through an authorized Owner or Agent may still be a real conformance deviation. Identify the required actor and do not exaggerate it as an untrusted exploit.

Countercheck repeated freeze/unfreeze cycles, partial and total freeze combinations, recovery of frozen balances, old/new wallet registry state, pause transitions, alternate entrypoints, proxy implementations, role changes, callback failures and reverted operations.

If the normative requirement, active implementation, authorization, deployment configuration, registry wiring or resulting state cannot be proven, use unresolved rather than possible_deviation.

steps.name: Review Roles, Interfaces, and Batch Variants
steps.content:
Objective: assess the roles_interfaces_batches requirements applicable to this mapped production component.

Shared normative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}. Routed requirement IDs: {{mapped_applicable_requirement_ids}}.

Use only catalogue records whose catalog_requirement_id appears in mapped_applicable_requirement_ids and whose domain is relevant to roles_interfaces_batches. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643.

Component context: ID {{mapped_component_id}}; label {{mapped_component_label}}; kind {{mapped_component_kind}}; source {{mapped_source_location}}; production entrypoints {{mapped_production_entrypoints}}; implementation chain {{mapped_implementation_chain}}; initialization {{mapped_initialization_path}}; roles {{mapped_roles}}; dependencies {{mapped_dependencies}}; wiring {{mapped_wiring}}; actor-controlled inputs {{mapped_actor_inputs}}; reachability evidence {{mapped_reachability_evidence}}; routed areas {{mapped_applicable_review_areas}}; scope status {{mapped_scope_status}}; uncertainty {{mapped_uncertainty}}.

If roles_interfaces_batches is not routed and no concrete evidence makes its applicability ambiguous, emit zero records. Do not mark a required role, function, event or batch variant not applicable merely because it is absent.

Review Owner and Agent authority across each ERC-3643 component according to its claimed standard role.

Trace:

* ERC-173 ownership initialization, visibility and transfer where applicable.
* Initial Owner assignment through constructors, initializers, factories and proxies.
* Agent addition, removal and membership queries.
* Owner authorization over Agent management where required.
* Agent authorization over each catalogue-governed operation.
* Role state after ownership transfers, upgrades and reinitialization.
* Direct, internal, delegated and inherited authorization paths.
* Required AgentAdded, AgentRemoved and ownership-related events.
* Whether removed Agents immediately lose the applicable authority.
* Whether authorized Agents retain the operations the standard requires them to perform.

Distinguish Owner authority from Agent authority. Do not assume that the Owner may directly execute every Agent-only operation unless the catalogue grants that authority or the Owner has also been appointed as an Agent. Do not treat the ability to appoint oneself as an Agent as a deviation when the standard permits it.

For Identity Registry Storage, distinguish an Owner-managed binding operation from the authority granted to bound Identity Registries. Do not require a particular role-library implementation, multisig, timelock or governance design. Assess externally observable authorization behavior rather than role names or internal architecture.

Compare the production-facing runtime surface with every routed official interface obligation, including IERC3643, IAgentRole, IIdentityRegistry, IIdentityRegistryStorage, ICompliance, ITrustedIssuersRegistry, IClaimTopicsRegistry, ERC-20 and ERC-173 as applicable.

For each required interface item verify:

* Function selector and ABI parameter types.
* Return types and required state mutability.
* Getter availability and returned representation.
* Event signature and indexed fields where specified.
* Runtime dispatch through proxies, inheritance and fallbacks.
* Executable behavior when the catalogue defines more than mere interface presence.

Apply Solidity and ABI compatibility rather than source-text equality. Parameter names, declaration order and a compatible public implementation of an external interface function are not deviations. Do not require ERC-165 support unless an applicable catalogue record explicitly requires it.

A proxy ABI artifact that omits an implementation function does not by itself prove runtime absence if the proxy correctly dispatches its selector. Conversely, interface inheritance, an ABI entry or a matching selector does not prove that the call reaches a conforming implementation or returns correctly encoded data.

Treat event declaration and event emission as separate questions. Require the event signature when catalogued; require emission, ordering or values only when an applicable behavioral requirement establishes them.

Inventory every routed batch function and trace:

* Caller and role authorization.
* Array arguments and correspondence between elements.
* Per-item identity, compliance, freeze, pause, balance and other validations inherited from the applicable single-operation semantics.
* Ordered state changes, callbacks and events.
* Interaction with internal single-operation helpers.
* Revert, return and partial-processing behavior only where the catalogue specifies it.
* Whether the batch exposes the same required substantive operation as its individual counterpart.

Do not invent array-length, atomicity, partial-success, gas or ordering requirements merely because they are common implementation choices. A single EVM transaction naturally executes within one block, but the standard’s batch requirement must be interpreted according to the exact catalogue obligation rather than assumed semantics.

Avoid duplicating the full behavioral analysis performed by the specialized siblings. Use their domains only as necessary to verify that role checks, interface exposure and batch routing preserve the catalogue-defined operation.

Emit one record per applicable atomic requirement with assessment_disposition equal to compliant, possible_deviation, not_applicable or unresolved.

Use not_applicable only when evidence proves that the requirement belongs to another component or role. Keep compliant records concise. A possible_deviation must include the exact requirement ID and source, expected and observed behavior, ABI or selector evidence, precise implementation locations, initialization and role state, ordered execution path, minimal call sequence, actor and controlled input, counterchecks, proportionate interoperability or authorization impact, exploitability and remaining uncertainty.

A conformance deviation may exist without an untrusted exploit, such as a missing required selector or an Agent operation that authorized integrations cannot call. Identify the actual impact without inflating it into a broader vulnerability.

Countercheck proxy targets, fallbacks, overloads, inherited implementations, alternate ABI exposure, initialization, reinitialization, ownership transfers, Agent removal, upgrades, direct and batch entrypoints, callback routing and reverted operations.

Exclude general access-control hardening, decentralization, governance and operational recommendations unless they directly prove a routed catalogue violation. If normative applicability, runtime dispatch, role state or production configuration cannot be proven, use unresolved rather than possible_deviation.

steps.name: Adjudicate and Deduplicate Proven Deviations
steps.content:
Objective: independently prove, countercheck and deduplicate possible ERC-3643 conformance deviations.

Shared authoritative catalogue: {{multi_output_depth_0}}.
Combined area assessments: {{multi_output_depth_2}}.

Repository context: {{repo_full}} at {{commit_sha}}; scope {{repo_scope}}; dependencies {{dependencies}}; configuration {{configuration}}; workspace root {{workspace_root}}; layout {{workspace_layout}}; manifest {{workspace_manifest_json}}.

Treat established depth-0 catalogue records as the only normative baseline. Do not reconstruct, reinterpret or broaden ERC-3643, and do not accept a requirement absent from the catalogue. A catalogue record marked unresolved_source cannot support a final finding.

Treat possible_deviation assessments as hypotheses. Use compliant, not_applicable and unresolved assessments, together with their preserved component IDs, execution paths, evidence locations and mapping uncertainties, to identify contradictions, alternate implementations, routing mistakes and missing evidence. A coverage gap or unresolved assessment is not itself a finding.

Before adjudicating candidates, verify that:

* Every candidate cites an established catalogue requirement.
* Its requirement was routed to the appropriate production-facing component.
* A missing expected function or subsystem was not incorrectly classified as not applicable.
* Multiple components or assessment areas have not reached contradictory conclusions about the same requirement.
* The candidate is not based on an optional feature, rationale, example or reference implementation behavior.

For each possible deviation independently verify:

1. The principal requirement ID, normative source, source anchor and binding strength.
2. The exact expected behavior without adding policy or implementation preferences.
3. The observed executable behavior or objectively missing production-facing interface surface.
4. The complete production route through proxies, implementations, inheritance, libraries, initialization, upgrades, roles, registries, identities, compliance contracts, dependencies and configuration.
5. The minimal pre-state, actor, inputs and ordered call or data-flow sequence.
6. Every relevant authorization, identity, claim, issuer, compliance, callback, pause, freeze, balance, allowance, registry and revert condition.
7. Alternate entrypoints, overloads, fallbacks, inherited implementations, proxy targets, feature gates, batch and individual variants.
8. Whether the candidate survives all counterchecks without relying on a material unresolved assumption.
9. The concrete conformance, interoperability or security consequence.
10. Whether an untrusted actor can practically trigger the behavior under the supplied production configuration.

Apply Solidity and ABI compatibility rather than source-text equality. Parameter names, declaration order and a compatible public implementation of an external interface function are not deviations. For proxy systems, distinguish an incomplete proxy ABI artifact from actual runtime selector absence. Interface inheritance, an ABI entry or a matching selector does not prove conforming execution.

A missing or ABI-incompatible required production-facing function can be proven as a conformance deviation without an exploit. For negative evidence, identify the expected selector, the inspected production-facing implementation and ABI, the relevant contract or proxy boundary, and the completed searches and counterchecks showing that no alternate dispatch path supplies it.

Reject a candidate when:

* Its catalogue record is unresolved_source.
* The cited text is optional, descriptive rationale or an example rather than binding.
* Applicability to the claimed ERC-3643 component is not established.
* Production reachability or active wiring is unsupported.
* The observed behavior cannot be distinguished from a valid Solidity or ABI implementation choice.
* A guard, inherited implementation, proxy target, alternate entrypoint or callback invalidates the reproduction.
* It relies on hypothetical configuration or legal-policy assumptions.
* It is merely a general security, economic, governance or architecture concern.
* Any assumption necessary to establish the deviation remains materially unresolved.

Deduplicate by root cause and nonconforming execution path, not merely by requirement ID or affected function. When one root cause violates several requirements, emit one finding with one principal finding_requirement_id and cite the related catalogue IDs in the explanation and evidence. Keep separate findings only when their causes, fixes or independently observable nonconforming outcomes are materially distinct.

A deviation reachable only through an authorized Owner or Agent may still be a valid conformance finding. Set exploitable to false when no untrusted actor can trigger it, identify the actual operational actor required, and do not portray standardized privileged functionality itself as malicious.

Emit one record per materially distinct proven deviation. Emit zero records if no candidate survives proof and counterchecks. Do not emit compliant results, unresolved concerns, coverage complaints, observations or placeholders as vulnerabilities.

For every emitted record populate:

* finding_requirement_id: principal established catalogue ID.
* finding_normative_source: exact official source and anchor.
* finding_expected_behavior: precise required behavior.
* finding_observed_behavior: proven production behavior.
* finding_evidence_locations: exact paths, lines, symbols, selectors, ABI and configuration facts.
* finding_reproduction_sequence: minimal ordered pre-state and execution sequence.
* finding_counterchecks: completed disproof attempts and their outcomes.
* finding_remaining_uncertainty: “none” when fully resolved, or only residual uncertainty that does not affect the conclusion.
* summary: concise statement of the deviation.
* explanation: requirement, root cause, observed mismatch, reachability, failed protections and proportionate impact.
* file_path: primary production source path.
* line: primary supporting line. For an absent function, use the nearest truthful production-facing contract, proxy dispatch or implementation boundary that supports the absence; never invent a line number.
* trigger_flow: ordered source locations and call or state transitions leading to the nonconforming result.
* vulnerability_type: “ERC-3643 conformance deviation — <domain>”.
* malicious_actor: realistic untrusted caller, required authorized actor, or “no malicious actor required”.
* malicious_input_example: concrete arguments and pre-state, or the authorized operational sequence when no malicious input exists.
* exploitable: true only when an untrusted actor can practically trigger the deviation under the supplied configuration.

Do not inflate a conformance defect into a security vulnerability. Whether findings are emitted or not, the result remains a structured first-pass ERC-3643 conformance analysis requiring professional auditor review.
